explanation: In Italy, light public displays of affection like hand-holding or a brief kiss on the cheek are generally acceptable in social gatherings, but passionate or prolonged kissing and intimate touching are considered inappropriate, especially in more formal or family-oriented settings. Italians value elegance and restraint in public, so overt displays can be seen as disrespectful or attention-seeking.
local_tip: Keep affection subtle: a quick kiss on the cheek as a greeting or hand-holding is fine, but avoid lingering embraces or kissing on the lips in mixed company.
regional_note: In southern Italy and more conservative areas (e.g., Sicily, Calabria), PDA is less tolerated, especially among older generations; in northern cities like Milan, attitudes are more relaxed.

also_check.note: Public displays of affection are illegal and can lead to arrest, even for married couples.
Kissing on the cheeks as a greeting and light PDA are very common and socially accepted.
Public displays of affection are highly discouraged; even holding hands can be seen as immodest.
